comments: Pattern syntax and semantics are Hydra-defined and translingual: they are specified once, in Hydra's regular-expression specification, and the same pattern means the same thing on every host.
Matching is leftmost-longest: a match begins at the earliest possible position in the string, and among the matches beginning at that position the longest is chosen.
findAll, replaceAll, and split operate on non-overlapping matches, found left to right.

metadata.description: Find the first regex match within a string, returning the matched substring if any.
comments: find(pat, s) returns Just(t) where t is the leftmost-longest substring of s matching pat, or Nothing if pat does not match anywhere in s.
Pattern syntax and semantics are Hydra-defined and translingual; see docs/specification/regex.md.
Total; a pattern that does not parse under the Hydra regex grammar is treated as not matching anywhere, the same as a well-formed pattern with no match.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.find.returnsLeftmostLongestMatch
provisions.statement: find returns the leftmost-longest substring matching the pattern, wrapped, when the pattern matches anywhere in the string, including alternation where the longer branch wins and greedy quantifiers that pick the longest run.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.find.noneWhenNoMatch
provisions.statement: find returns none when the pattern does not match anywhere in the string, including on the empty string, and when the pattern is ill-formed under the Hydra regex grammar (treated the same as a well-formed pattern with no match, never a host-specific parse error).

parameters.name: pat
parameters.description: the regex pattern to search for

metadata.description: Find all non-overlapping regex matches within a string.
comments: findAll(pat, s) returns the list of all leftmost-longest, non-overlapping matches of pat in s, in the order they appear. Returns the empty list if pat does not match anywhere.
Pattern syntax and semantics are Hydra-defined and translingual; see docs/specification/regex.md.
Total; an unparseable pattern yields the empty list, the same as a well-formed pattern with no matches.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.findAll.returnsAllNonOverlappingMatchesInOrder
provisions.statement: findAll returns every leftmost-longest, non-overlapping match of the pattern in the string, in the order they appear.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.findAll.emptyListWhenNoMatch
provisions.statement: findAll returns the empty list when the pattern does not match anywhere, including when the pattern is ill-formed under the Hydra regex grammar (treated the same as a well-formed pattern with no matches).

parameters.name: pat
parameters.description: the regex pattern to search for

metadata.description: Test whether a regex matches an entire string.
comments: matches(pat, s) returns true iff pat matches the whole of s (anchored at both ends; a match of a proper substring of s does not suffice). To test whether pat matches anywhere within s, use find.
Pattern syntax and semantics are Hydra-defined and translingual; see docs/specification/regex.md.
Total; an unparseable pattern yields false, the same as a well-formed pattern with no match.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.matches.isWholeStringAnchored
provisions.statement: matches is always anchored to the whole string at both ends, regardless of explicit ^/$ in the pattern: a match of a proper substring does not suffice, and ^/$ never match at an internal line break (string-boundary anchors, not line-boundary).

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.matches.testsMinimalCoreGrammar
provisions.statement: matches correctly evaluates every construct in the minimal-core regex grammar: literals, character classes (including negation and ranges), the wildcard (matching any character including newline), quantifiers (?, *, +, {n}, {n,}, {n,m}), alternation (leftmost-longest preference, not leftmost-first), and non-capturing grouping (including nested and quantified groups).

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.matches.treatsEscapedMetacharactersAsLiterals
provisions.statement: matches treats a backslash-escaped metacharacter as the literal character, both at top level and inside a character class, and treats an unescaped dash as a literal at top level (never forming a range outside a class) while forming a range only inside a class.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.matches.falseWhenNoMatchOrIllFormed
provisions.statement: matches returns false when the pattern does not match the whole string, including when the pattern is ill-formed under the Hydra regex grammar (treated the same as a well-formed pattern with no match, never a host-specific parse error) and for constructs outside the minimal core (such as the {,m} quantifier form).

metadata.description: Replace the first regex match in a string with a replacement string.
comments: replace(pat, repl, s) returns s with the first leftmost-longest match of pat replaced by repl. If pat does not match, s is returned unchanged.
Replacement-string syntax (capture-group references such as $1 or \\1, literal escapes) is host-defined.
Pattern syntax and semantics are Hydra-defined and translingual; see docs/specification/regex.md.
Total; an unparseable pattern leaves s unchanged, the same as a well-formed pattern with no match.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.replace.replacesLeftmostLongestMatch
provisions.statement: replace replaces the first (leftmost-longest) match of the pattern with the replacement string, including an anchored match at the start of the string.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.replace.unchangedWhenNoMatch
provisions.statement: replace returns the string unchanged when the pattern does not match anywhere, including when the pattern is ill-formed under the Hydra regex grammar (treated the same as a well-formed pattern with no match).

metadata.description: Replace all non-overlapping regex matches in a string with a replacement string.
comments: replaceAll(pat, repl, s) returns s with every leftmost-longest, non-overlapping match of pat replaced by repl. If pat does not match anywhere, s is returned unchanged.
Replacement-string syntax is host-defined; see replace for the caveat.
Pattern syntax and semantics are Hydra-defined and translingual; see docs/specification/regex.md.
Total; an unparseable pattern leaves s unchanged, the same as a well-formed pattern with no match.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.replaceAll.replacesEveryNonOverlappingMatch
provisions.statement: replaceAll replaces every leftmost-longest, non-overlapping match of the pattern with the replacement string, including when the replacement string is empty.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.replaceAll.unchangedWhenNoMatch
provisions.statement: replaceAll returns the string unchanged when the pattern does not match anywhere, including when the pattern is ill-formed under the Hydra regex grammar (treated the same as a well-formed pattern with no match).

metadata.description: Split a string by occurrences of a regex pattern.
comments: split(pat, s) returns the list of substrings of s obtained by splitting on every leftmost-longest, non-overlapping match of pat.
Trailing empty splits are host-defined (some engines retain them, some discard them; for portable code, do not rely on the trailing-empty behavior).
Pattern syntax and semantics are Hydra-defined and translingual; see docs/specification/regex.md.
Total; an unparseable pattern yields the single-element list containing s, the same as a well-formed pattern with no match.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.split.splitsOnEveryNonOverlappingMatch
provisions.statement: split returns the substrings of the string obtained by splitting on every leftmost-longest, non-overlapping match of the pattern, including splitting on a fixed delimiter, on a character class, and splitting into a trailing empty substring when the pattern matches at the end of the string.

provisions.name: hydra.core.lib.regex.split.singleElementListWhenNoMatchOrIllFormed
provisions.statement: split returns the single-element list containing the original string unchanged when the pattern does not match anywhere, including when the pattern is ill-formed under the Hydra regex grammar (treated the same as a well-formed pattern with no match).

parameters.name: pat
parameters.description: the regex pattern to split on
